newsitem.title: USA: Abortion foe Salvi buried, victim attends funeral.
newsitem.headline: Abortion foe Salvi buried, victim attends funeral.

text.p: Abortion foe John Salvi, convicted for the shootings deaths of two health clinic workers and the wounding of five others in what was the worst violence at abortion clinics in the nation, was buried Wednesday.

Salvi, 24, was found dead, an apparent suicide, Friday in his cell at Massachusetts' maximum security prison in Walpole where he was serving more than two life terms for the shootings at two health clinics in the Boston suburb of Brookline.
Among the 80 mourners at St. Stanisalaus Church in Ipswich, a small community 25 miles northeast of Boston, was one of Salvi's victims, security guard Richard Serone.
"I don't hold the parents responsible for what happened," Serone told reporters. "It was the mental illness, not the man, not his family, not his upbringing. That's my view."

Massachusetts Gov. William Weld has ordered an expanded probe into Salvi's death and his family has demanded a federal investigation to find out why he was sent to a maximum security prison and not to another prison where he could have received more mental health treatment.
